$comment: Single source of truth for every per-environment value in this deployment.
Three consumers read this file, and a test (src/infra/environments.test.ts)
fails when any of them drifts from it:
1. Terraform (infra/cloudflare) provisions the Cloudflare resources.
2. wrangler.toml declares the Worker that runs inside them.
3. scripts/cloudflare-access.mjs and scripts/cloudflare-r2.mjs verify the
invariants that live in Cloudflare rather than in code.
Nothing secret belongs here. It is tracked, and the secret scan in CI reads
every tracked file. Credentials reach Terraform through the environment and
reach the Worker through `wrangler secret`.
To add an environment: add an entry below, add
infra/cloudflare/environments/<env>.tfvars and <env>.backend.hcl, and add the
matching [env.<wranglerEnv>] section to wrangler.toml. The drift test iterates
this file, so a new entry immediately requires the rest to exist.
The [env.<name>] block in wrangler.toml that configures this
environment, and the value every wrangler invocation passes as --env.
There is no implicit default: wrangler.toml sets no top-level `main`,
so a deploy that forgets --env fails rather than publishing this Worker
with no routes, no vars and no bindings over the live script.
That block MUST set `name` explicitly. Wrangler otherwise appends the
environment to the Worker name and publishes a NEW Worker, with new
Durable Objects -- so every room and every account is simply not there.
$comment_hostnames: Single-label subdomains are deliberate: Cloudflare Universal SSL covers
the apex and *.<zone> only, so app.playground.<zone> would get no
certificate. The teacher host is the ONLY one an Access application may

$comment: audience is the application AUD Cloudflare generates. It is an output of
the Terraform stack, not an input: apply the stack, read
`terraform output access_application_aud`, and write it here. The Worker
rejects every token when it disagrees, and `npm run access:check` compares
this value against the live application.
$comment_organizationName: The Zero Trust team name, as the dashboard shows it. Null until an
owner reads the real value: cloudflare_zero_trust_organization requires
it, and guessing would rename the account-wide organization as a side
effect of a branding change. manage_login_branding stays false in
prod.tfvars until this is filled in.

$comment: One bucket for the whole environment. The isolation primitive is the room
grant, not the bucket; the one axis that does deserve separate buckets is
the environment, so staging cannot read or overwrite production's images.
locationHint is uppercase for the Terraform provider; the Cloudflare REST
API used by scripts/cloudflare-r2.mjs takes the lowercase form.
Cloudflare Access free-plan seat budget. A brand-new tutor account is
refused at this count; an existing tutor is never refused.
Edge rate limit on POST /auth/guest, on the guest hostname only. This is
the outer bound that sheds volumetric abuse before a Worker invocation is
billed. It is deliberately far looser than GUEST_AUTH_RATE_MAX (5/min per
IP, src/lib/worker/rateLimits.ts), which stays the real product limit --
so the edge rule never trips before the in-Worker limiter does for a
legitimate client, and a legitimate client's refusal is always the
Worker's considered 429 rather than an opaque edge block.
The zone's free plan allows exactly one rate-limit rule. This is it.
periodSeconds is 10 because it is the ONLY period this plan entitles.
The API refuses anything else: 'not entitled to use the period 60, can
only use a period among [10]'. 20 per 10s is 120/min, still far looser
than the Worker's 5/min, which keeps the product limit the deciding one.
mitigationTimeoutSeconds is 10 for the same reason: the API says 'not
entitled to use a mitigation timeout different from 10'. Both numbers are
the plan's, not a choice this repository gets to make.
Owned and published by the fork repository, which is the sole owner of the
bucket, custom domain, and release objects. This repository only consumes
the pinned immutable base URL, so no Terraform resource here manages it.
assetOrigin feeds the Worker's CSP font-src; assetBaseUrl is inlined into
the static export at build time.
